name: tartar sauce
instructions:
Classical tartar sauce — mayonnaise base with finely chopped dill pickles, lemon juice, dijon mustard, capers, shallot, and fresh dill. Mix everything in a bowl, let sit at least 15-30 min for the flavors to meld. Serve cold.

=== INGREDIENTS (makes about 3/4 cup) ===

- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 2 tbsp DILL PICKLES, very finely chopped
- 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice
- 1 tsp dijon mustard
- 1 tsp BRINED CAPERS, drained and finely chopped (optional but classical)
- 1 tbsp shallot (or red onion), very finely minced
- 1 tbsp fresh dill, chopped (or 1 tbsp fresh parsley if no dill)
- salt and black pepper to taste

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Combine everything in a small bowl.
2. Whisk / stir to combine evenly.
3. Cover and refrigerate at least 15-30 min before serving — the pickle, dijon, and lemon need time to meld into the mayo base.
4. Serve cold as a dipping sauce.
notes:
Classical tartar sauce. Standard companion to fried fish, breaded chicken (especially chicken-schnitzel — see PAIRINGS), and other fried/breaded proteins.

=== MAYO IS THE BASE — DON'T SUBSTITUTE ===

Mayonnaise is the load-bearing base. Sour cream, greek yogurt, or crème fraîche don't sub cleanly — the tanginess is different and the emulsion structure doesn't hold the same way. Full-fat mayo is standard.

=== DILL PICKLES — FINELY CHOPPED, NOT SWEET PICKLES ===

DILL pickles (not sweet / bread-and-butter pickles). Very finely chopped so they distribute evenly through the sauce rather than sitting as discrete chunks. Pickle relish (already chopped) is a fine shortcut — use dill relish specifically, not sweet relish.

=== LEMON JUICE IS THE BRIGHTNESS AXIS ===

Fresh lemon juice, not vinegar. The pickles are already contributing brine acid; lemon juice adds a brighter, cleaner citrus note that layers on top rather than doubling down on the pickle brine.

=== CAPERS ARE CLASSICAL BUT OPTIONAL ===

Capers add a briny-fermented pop that pairs with the pickles. Classical inclusion but skippable if you don't have any / don't like capers.

=== SHALLOT OVER RED ONION ===

Shallot is milder and more elegant than raw red onion; the sauce sits in a delicate register. Red onion works but reads more aggressive.

=== LET IT SIT ===

15-30 min in the fridge before serving is what lets the flavors integrate. Freshly-made tartar sauce tastes like separate ingredients; rested tartar sauce tastes like tartar sauce.

=== PAIRINGS ===

- CHICKEN-SCHNITZEL: primary pairing (see chicken-schnitzel). Tartar sauce + a lemon wedge on the side is the classical schnitzel dip.
- FRIED FISH: canonical use case.
- CHICKEN-TENDERS: not the pick — tenders favor honey / barbecue dips (see chicken-tenders). Tartar sauce's dill + pickle register reads wrong against the standard tender-and-fries american-comfort context.
- FREEZER FRIES: works, especially when serving with schnitzel — dip both the schnitzel and the fries in the same sauce.
